{"parentUuid":"71d1f511-0afa-486e-bf46-415a0a7a6d78","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"mcp_instructions_delta","addedNames":["plugin:context7:context7","plugin:serena:serena"],"addedBlocks":["## plugin:context7:context7\nUse this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service -- even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer -- your training data may not reflect recent changes. {"parentUuid":"6fcafcea-486d-4155-9a3c-6229cb0247df","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Use when planning multi-step work where some sub-tasks are mechanical (file ops, regex, count, schema validation) and others require judgment (synthesis, design, ambiguity resolution). Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- empirical-probe-first: Probe ALL viable strategies in a multi-option ladder BEFORE committing to one. Use when a session-plan / decision-ADR / spec presents ≥3 strategy options (e.g. \"Strategy A1/A2/A3\" or \"alternative B/C/D\") and the recommended option's source-evidence may be stale. Outputs a probe matrix per strategy + commit decision with empirical citation. Pairs with `vendor-api-probe.sh` (deterministic detection layer; SessionStart hook) and `decompose-work` (deterministic-vs-LLM split per probe). Charter promotion target — codifies L-S32-1 doctrine surfaced at S32 Track A pivot (master-plan recommended A2 vnstock alternate; empirical probe rejected A1+A2; A3 SSI direct httpx adopted instead).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n- fastapi-module: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\n- hook-diagnostics: Inspect hook event lifecycle (state machine + transcript cache + aggregator output) when triaging failed/stuck hooks or auditing self-awareness rollups. Use during sandwich-verifier review, drift investigation, or post-mortem when component-telemetry.jsonl + dispatch.jsonl + sessions-rollup.tsv need cross-checking.\n- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the StockForge Obsidian vault with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index maintenance. Use when adding content to the knowledge base, navigating entities/concepts, or maintaining the raw/wiki separation. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed. Extended with raw/wiki pattern from Karpathy LLM Wiki.\n- postgres-pgvector: Design Postgres schemas with pgvector and TimescaleDB for StockForge. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n- promote-rule: Cluster agent-notes.md entries by lexical similarity, propose promotion of recurring rules to deterministic hook (priority 1), skill (priority 2), or charter (priority 3). Use when agent-notes has accumulated ≥10 new rules since last promotion run, or on-demand at phase boundary. Outputs proposal markdown to observations/. Pairs with capability-map.md (writes new task_class entries) and decompose-work (consumes promotion outcomes).\n- prompt-engineering: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\n- qa-escalation: File-based Q&A protocol — composes bundle file in human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, tracks lifecycle (pending → answered → stale → processed), creates URGENT notification when needed. Use when intent classifier recommends OPEN_QA_BUNDLE / ESCALATE_HUMAN, or grill-maximization has a bundle ready to write. Pairs with grill-maximization (composes content) + Track 5 hooks (auto-move stale).\n- session-memory-l0-l1: Extract structured memories (L0 quick metadata + L1 deep) from a Claude Code session JSONL transcript. L0 is pure regex (file paths, commands, errors, failures incl. Vietnamese phrases, next step). L1 ships the prompt builder + response parser + 15+35 head/tail windowing — caller dispatches the LLM (no auto-invoke in Phase 0). Plus cleanText harness-stripper + TranscriptCache (mtime+size dual-check + LRU). Use when ingesting a session for memory promotion, computing what files/commands/failures the session touched, or preparing an offline LLM extraction.\n- spec-dual-layer: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n- spec-to-wiki: Convert raw specifications to Obsidian wiki format with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index updates. Use when adding a new spec to the knowledge base, or when regenerating wiki view after spec changes. Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n- sync-pull: On-demand confidence-score lookup before a SCOPE+/ARCH/IMPL decision. Reads agent-workspace/memory/sync-tracker/state.tsv + weights.yaml; surfaces the relevant category's score, tier, must-grill flag, and the decision-class threshold. Output drives \"self-decide vs grill\" choice. Use whenever an agent is about to commit a non-trivial decision and needs to ground confidence in historical hit rate per Charter Principle 8 (Calibration over confidence).\n- test-pyramid-balance: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. Use when deciding what test to write, reviewing test coverage, or rebalancing skewed test suite. Covers test pyramid shape, BDD vs unit tests, when to use what. Includes stock-domain-specific test categories.\n- try-n-approaches: Karpathy autoresearch outer-loop framing — given a task or signal, generate ≥3 distinct approaches (DEEPEN / BROADEN / ABANDON families), pick one per cheap-first ordering, attach a deterministic metric function (per L-S12-1), and write the experiment frame to learning-data/loop/. Use when an open question surfaces from drift / dogfood / sync-grilling and you need to commit a measurable next step. {"parentUuid":"216fff32-d314-4cbb-b5a5-231d05903e7f","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"37b5d64d-e9c9-4b01-9c5e-576617ce6a93","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_012icwtQm3WsQRgmsirH1pkR","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t---\n2\tproposal_id: decision-discipline-amendment-rule-4b\n3\ttitle: Decision-discipline Rule 4b — Lesson-synthesis mandatory at session-end (charter-tier amendment draft)\n4\tstatus: PROPOSAL\n5\tdraft_date: 2026-05-04\n6\tdraft_session: S43e\n7\tauthoring_agent: Claude Opus 4.7\n8\ttarget_charter_file: agent-workspace/constitution/decision-discipline.md\n9\tgating: USER-EXPLICIT-PICK-REQUIRED (per Q-B2 charter-tier rule + L-S15-1)\n10\tprovenance:\n11\t  promote_rule_observation: agent-workspace/memory/observations/promote-rule-S43c.md § Cluster C2\n12\t  source_rules:\n13\t    - KI-S35-5  # 15-session promote-skip\n14\t    - BP-S35-1  # 5-session-or-phase-boundary\n15\t    - KI-S43b-5  # 9-session lesson-synthesis dormancy\n16\t    - BP-S43b-4  # lesson-synthesis mandatory\n17\t    - L-S43b-7   # Lesson-Synthesis Stage 2 Of Self-Upgrade Loop Has No Agent\n18\t  related_hooks_already_deployed:\n19\t    - scripts/hooks/lesson-synthesis-watchdog.sh  # advisory mode (HR-1)\n20\t    - scripts/hooks/promotion-cycle-trigger.sh    # delta-since-last hard-block at 5+\n21\t    - scripts/hooks/harness-recovery-dod-watchdog.sh  # premature-stop sentinel\n22\t    - scripts/hooks/memory-routing-audit.sh        # HR-4 routing-tree\n23\t    - scripts/hooks/pre-clear-handoff-guard.sh     # HR-2 / HR-7\n24\t---\n25\t\n26\t# Proposal: Decision-discipline Rule 4b — Lesson-synthesis mandatory at session-end\n27\t\n28\t> **Status**: DRAFT — proposed for charter ratification at user discretion.\n29\t> **Tier**: CHARTER (per L-S15-1: any rule reshaping self-upgrade-loop identity is charter-tier).\n30\t> **Required action**: User explicit letter pick per Q-B2 closure (charter/SCOPE-tier MUST require explicit accept; default-acceptance prohibited).\n31\t\n32\t## Why this rule exists\n33\t\n34\tThe self-upgrade loop (Karpathy outer-loop / decision-discipline § Rule 4) requires\n35\tthat lessons learned in real sessions feed back into KI-* / BP-* / agent-notes\n36\tentries, which then promote up to hooks / skills / charter via Rule 4 (5-session OR\n37\tphase-boundary). Empirically, Stage 2 (the *write-the-lesson-down* step itself) has\n38\tbeen the dormancy hotspot:\n39\t\n40\t- **S20 → S35**: 15 sessions elapsed before promote-rule fired (KI-S35-5).\n41\t- **S26 → S43b**: 9 sessions elapsed before lesson-synthesizer ran (KI-S43b-5).\n42\t- **L-S43b-7**: cataloged the failure mode — \"Stage 2 of Self-Upgrade Loop Has No Agent\".\n43\t\n44\tStage 1 (rule-discovery during work) is implicit in good engineering. Stage 2\n45\t(rule-recording) is the bottleneck. Without a deterministic rule forcing it,\n46\tsessions complete without synthesizing learnings, the corpus stagnates, and\n47\tpromote-rule cycles surface a thin set of stale candidates.\n48\t\n49\t## Proposed amendment text\n50\t\n51\tAppend to `agent-workspace/constitution/decision-discipline.md` § Rule 4 region:\n52\t\n53\t```markdown\n54\t### Rule 4b — Lesson-synthesis mandatory at session-end\n55\t\n56\tEvery session whose work produces ANY of the following triggers MUST append at\n57\tleast one new entry to `agent-workspace/memory/self-awareness/known-issues.md`\n58\tOR `agent-workspace/memory/self-awareness/best-practices.md` OR\n59\t`agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md` BEFORE the checkpoint `latest.md` is\n60\twritten:\n61\t\n62\t  (a) ≥1 user correction (verbatim or paraphrased)\n63\t  (b) ≥1 deferred-fix item (R-N / DEFER-S*-N)\n64\t  (c) ≥1 substrate gap discovered (hook missing, contract unenforced, etc.)\n65\t  (d) ≥1 charter-tier or SCOPE-tier decision authored\n66\t  (e) ≥1 META_LOOP recovery action\n67\t\n68\tThe entry MUST cite at minimum: (i) verbatim trigger evidence; (ii) the rule it\n69\tcodifies; (iii) anti-example (what the rule prevents); (iv) auto-detect path\n70\t(hook / skill / charter). Sessions producing zero triggers (e.g., rote refactor\n71\tsessions) are exempt and SHOULD record `lesson_synthesis: NA-no-triggers` in\n72\ttheir session log.\n73\t\n74\t**Enforcement** (paired hook upgrade):\n75\t  - `scripts/hooks/lesson-synthesis-watchdog.sh` is promoted from advisory\n76\t    (current default) to STRICT mode (exit 2 on dormancy detection).\n77\t  - Strict mode auto-clears once the next session writes a qualifying entry.\n78\t  - Loop is finite: ≤1 hard-block per dormancy episode.\n79\t\n80\t**Cross-references**: KI-S35-5, BP-S35-1, KI-S43b-5, BP-S43b-4, L-S43b-7.\n81\t**Supersedes**: nothing (additive to Rule 4).\n82\t**Companion**: Rule 4 promote-rule cadence remains 5-session OR phase-boundary;\n83\tthis rule shortens the *upstream* feedback latency that feeds Rule 4.\n84\t```\n85\t\n86\t## Why charter-tier (not skill, not just hook)\n87\t\n88\tPer Q-E3 promotion priority (closed S15) — hook FIRST, skill SECOND, charter LAST.\n89\tThis proposal lands at charter because:\n90\t\n91\t1. **The hook already exists** (`lesson-synthesis-watchdog.sh`) but is advisory-only.\n92\t   Promoting it to strict-mode requires a charter-tier rule to cite as authority.\n93\t2. **The pattern reshapes self-upgrade-loop identity** — it codifies *that* the loop\n94\t   has a Stage 2 obligation, not merely *how* to enforce it. That's identity-level\n95\t   (per L-S15-1 charter-split rule).\n96\t3. **Skill insufficient** — this is a discipline rule, not a procedure. There is no\n97\t   sequence of LLM-judgment-required steps; the rule is \"write or be blocked\".\n98\t\n99\t## Trade-offs\n100\t\n101\t| Concern | Mitigation |\n102\t|---|---|\n103\t| **False-positive blocks on rote sessions** | Exemption clause `lesson_synthesis: NA-no-triggers` + 5 explicit trigger gates (a)-(e); rote refactor sessions self-attest exemption. |\n104\t| **Verbose KI/BP corpus growth** | Rule 4 promote-rule cadence (5-session OR phase-boundary) prunes via cluster-and-promote; growth pressure is already balanced by demote pressure. |\n105\t| **Strict-mode hard-block surprise** | Loop is finite (≤1 per episode); exit 2 surfaces stderr to assistant transcript per HR-7 pattern; agent writes entry → next Stop auto-clears. |\n106\t| **Watchdog itself dormant** | Hook is in `.claude/settings.json` Stop chain priority 12 (already deployed); strict-mode upgrade is a 1-line change in the script. |\n107\t\n108\t## Failure modes if NOT ratified\n109\t\n110\t- Recurrence: 6+ sessions of dormancy expected within next phase based on KI-S43b-5\n111\t  empirical baseline.\n112\t- Compounding: stale promote-rule candidate pool → low-quality cluster proposals →\n113\t  stale charter → meta-loop trust loss (per L-S43b-10 premature-stop family).\n114\t\n115\t## What ratification looks like (for the user)\n116\t\n117\tIf the user picks \"ACCEPT\":\n118\t1. Agent moves this file to `agent-workspace/constitution/decision-discipline.md` via\n119\t   the S38 deny-lift mechanism (charter-edit gate).\n120\t2. Agent appends the amendment text verbatim under § Rule 4 region.\n121\t3. Agent flips `lesson-synthesis-watchdog.sh` from advisory to strict (1-line edit:\n122\t   `exit 0` → `exit 2` on dormancy branch).\n123\t4. Agent authors `D-NNN-decision-discipline-rule-4b-ratified.md` ADR with\n124\t   approval_chain pointing to the user pick.\n125\t\n126\tIf the user picks \"REJECT\":\n127\t1. scripts/hooks/memory-routing-audit.sh        # HR-4 routing-tree\n    - scripts/hooks/pre-clear-handoff-guard.sh     # HR-2 / HR-7\n---\n\n# Proposal: Decision-discipline Rule 4b — Lesson-synthesis mandatory at session-end\n\n> **Status**: DRAFT — proposed for charter ratification at user discretion.\n> **Tier**: CHARTER (per L-S15-1: any rule reshaping self-upgrade-loop identity is charter-tier).\n> **Required action**: User explicit letter pick per Q-B2 closure (charter/SCOPE-tier MUST require explicit accept; default-acceptance prohibited).\n\n## Why this rule exists\n\nThe self-upgrade loop (Karpathy outer-loop / decision-discipline § Rule 4) requires\nthat lessons learned in real sessions feed back into KI-* / BP-* / agent-notes\nentries, which then promote up to hooks / skills / charter via Rule 4 (5-session OR\nphase-boundary). Empirically, Stage 2 (the *write-the-lesson-down* step itself) has\nbeen the dormancy hotspot:\n\n- **S20 → S35**: 15 sessions elapsed before promote-rule fired (KI-S35-5).\n- **S26 → S43b**: 9 sessions elapsed before lesson-synthesizer ran (KI-S43b-5).\n- **L-S43b-7**: cataloged the failure mode — \"Stage 2 of Self-Upgrade Loop Has No Agent\".\n\nStage 1 (rule-discovery during work) is implicit in good engineering. Stage 2\n(rule-recording) is the bottleneck. Without a deterministic rule forcing it,\nsessions complete without synthesizing learnings, the corpus stagnates, and\npromote-rule cycles surface a thin set of stale candidates.\n\n## Proposed amendment text\n\nAppend to `agent-workspace/constitution/decision-discipline.md` § Rule 4 region:\n\n```markdown\n### Rule 4b — Lesson-synthesis mandatory at session-end\n\nEvery session whose work produces ANY of the following triggers MUST append at\nleast one new entry to `agent-workspace/memory/self-awareness/known-issues.md`\nOR `agent-workspace/memory/self-awareness/best-practices.md` OR\n`agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md` BEFORE the checkpoint `latest.md` is\nwritten:\n\n  (a) ≥1 user correction (verbatim or paraphrased)\n  (b) ≥1 deferred-fix item (R-N / DEFER-S*-N)\n  (c) ≥1 substrate gap discovered (hook missing, contract unenforced, etc.)\n  (d) ≥1 charter-tier or SCOPE-tier decision authored\n  (e) ≥1 META_LOOP recovery action\n\nThe entry MUST cite at minimum: (i) verbatim trigger evidence; (ii) the rule it\ncodifies; (iii) anti-example (what the rule prevents); (iv) auto-detect path\n(hook / skill / charter). Sessions producing zero triggers (e.g., rote refactor\nsessions) are exempt and SHOULD record `lesson_synthesis: NA-no-triggers` in\ntheir session log.\n\n**Enforcement** (paired hook upgrade):\n  - `scripts/hooks/lesson-synthesis-watchdog.sh` is promoted from advisory\n    (current default) to STRICT mode (exit 2 on dormancy detection).\n  - Strict mode auto-clears once the next session writes a qualifying entry.\n  - Loop is finite: ≤1 hard-block per dormancy episode.\n\n**Cross-references**: KI-S35-5, BP-S35-1, KI-S43b-5, BP-S43b-4, L-S43b-7.\n**Supersedes**: nothing (additive to Rule 4).\n**Companion**: Rule 4 promote-rule cadence remains 5-session OR phase-boundary;\nthis rule shortens the *upstream* feedback latency that feeds Rule 4.\n```\n\n## Why charter-tier (not skill, not just hook)\n\nPer Q-E3 promotion priority (closed S15) — hook FIRST, skill SECOND, charter LAST.\nThis proposal lands at charter because:\n\n1. **The hook already exists** (`lesson-synthesis-watchdog.sh`) but is advisory-only.\n   Promoting it to strict-mode requires a charter-tier rule to cite as authority.\n2. **The pattern reshapes self-upgrade-loop identity** — it codifies *that* the loop\n   has a Stage 2 obligation, not merely *how* to enforce it. That's identity-level\n   (per L-S15-1 charter-split rule).\n3. **Skill insufficient** — this is a discipline rule, not a procedure. There is no\n   sequence of LLM-judgment-required steps; the rule is \"write or be blocked\".\n\n## Trade-offs\n\n| Concern | Mitigation |\n|---|---|\n| **False-positive blocks on rote sessions** | Exemption clause `lesson_synthesis: NA-no-triggers` + 5 explicit trigger gates (a)-(e); rote refactor sessions self-attest exemption. |\n| **Verbose KI/BP corpus growth** | Rule 4 promote-rule cadence (5-session OR phase-boundary) prunes via cluster-and-promote; growth pressure is already balanced by demote pressure. |\n| **Strict-mode hard-block surprise** | Loop is finite (≤1 per episode); exit 2 surfaces stderr to assistant transcript per HR-7 pattern; agent writes entry → next Stop auto-clears. |\n| **Watchdog itself dormant** | Hook is in `.claude/settings.json` Stop chain priority 12 (already deployed); strict-mode upgrade is a 1-line change in the script. |\n\n## Failure modes if NOT ratified\n\n- Recurrence: 6+ sessions of dormancy expected within next phase based on KI-S43b-5\n  empirical baseline.\n- Compounding: stale promote-rule candidate pool → low-quality cluster proposals →\n  stale charter → meta-loop trust loss (per L-S43b-10 premature-stop family).\n\n## What ratification looks like (for the user)\n\nIf the user picks \"ACCEPT\":\n1. Edits require explicit user prompt + Q&A per `agent-workspace/CLAUDE.md` constitution-amendment process.\n20\t\n21\t## Purpose\n22\t\n23\tCodify how decisions get made, how learned rules get promoted, and where the agent has IMPL-tier discretion vs where the agent MUST surface explicit user picks. Resolves the recurring failure mode of (a) silent default-acceptance on charter-tier scope (UP-06 NO Silent File-Defaults) and (b) churn from over-promoting routine rules to charter when a hook would suffice (Q-E3).\n24\t\n25\t## Rule 1 — Tier-vs-Default-Acceptance (Q-B2 — closed Recommended)\n26\t\n27\tA decision's **tier** determines whether default-acceptance is permissible:\n28\t\n29\t| Tier | Default-acceptance allowed? | Mechanism |\n30\t|---|---|---|\n31\t| **CHARTER** | NO — MUST require explicit user letter pick | AskUserQuestion with no auto-fallback; SessionEnd does NOT close the question |\n32\t| **SCOPE** | NO — MUST require explicit user letter pick | AskUserQuestion with no auto-fallback; born-answered Q&A bundle if user offline |\n33\t| **DECISION_ROUTING** | NO (paired with SCOPE per Q-B2 reasoning) | AskUserQuestion explicit pick |\n34\t| **ARCH** | YES with caveat — explicit pick preferred; agent default with transparent flag if user unavailable | Document the default in decision file frontmatter |\n35\t| **IMPL** | YES — agent decides per L-S11-2 doctrine | Routine implementation choice; log in session journal only |\n36\t\n37\t**Anti-pattern**: bundling a CHARTER-tier item with sub-charter-tier items in one Q&A. Surface the divergence as a REV-N amendment to the parent decision; do NOT churn downstream.\n51\t\n52\t**Carry-over examples**: D-005 REV-1 ratifies IMPL-S11-2 (path layout) + IMPL-S12-1 (dogfood file split) per this doctrine.\n53\t\n54\t**Anti-pattern**: rewriting the parent decision's prose to match every IMPL nudge. Advisory exit 0; emits\n# alert to stderr + log so the agent sees it before /clear or session-end.\n#\n# Bash + POSIX only per L-S11-1.\n# Stop hook (priority 2 — after self-awareness-aggregate, before promotion-cycle).\n# Decision basis: KI-S43b-5 (9-session dormant loop) + BP-S43b-4 promotion target.\n\nset -uo pipefail\ntrap 'exit 0' ERR\n\nPROJECT_DIR=\"${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}\"\nMEM_DIR=\"$PROJECT_DIR/agent-workspace/memory\"\nSA_DIR=\"$MEM_DIR/self-awareness\"\nLOG=\"$MEM_DIR/.lesson-synthesis.log\"\nHOOK_LOG=\"$MEM_DIR/.session-hooks.log\"\nTS=\"$(date -Iseconds)\"\n\nmkdir -p \"$(dirname \"$LOG\")\"\n\n# Scope: count files touched in production tree (staged + unstaged + untracked).\n# git status --short gives one line per touched file regardless of state.\nPROD_TOUCHED=$(cd \"$PROJECT_DIR\" && git status --short -- packages/ apps/ 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]')\n[[ \"$PROD_TOUCHED\" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || PROD_TOUCHED=0\n\n# Threshold: if 0 files touched, no lesson expected\nif [ \"$PROD_TOUCHED\" -lt 1 ]; then\n  printf '[%s] lesson-synthesis-watchdog: prod_touched=%s files (under threshold; skip)\\n' \\\n    \"$TS\" \"$PROD_TOUCHED\" >> \"$LOG\"\n  exit 0\nfi\n\n# Were any of the lesson-target files updated in last 24h?\nKI_RECENT=$(find \"$SA_DIR/known-issues.md\" -mtime -1 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]')\nBP_RECENT=$(find \"$SA_DIR/best-practices.md\" -mtime -1 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]')\nNOTES_RECENT=$(find \"$MEM_DIR/agent-notes.md\" -mtime -1 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]')\n\nLESSON_TOTAL=$(( KI_RECENT + BP_RECENT + NOTES_RECENT ))\n\nprintf '[%s] lesson-synthesis-watchdog: prod_touched=%s ki_recent=%s bp_recent=%s notes_recent=%s\\n' \\\n  \"$TS\" \"$PROD_TOUCHED\" \"$KI_RECENT\" \"$BP_RECENT\" \"$NOTES_RECENT\" >> \"$LOG\"\n\nif [ \"$LESSON_TOTAL\" -eq 0 ]; then\n  ALERT=\"lesson-synthesis-watchdog ALERT: production files touched = $PROD_TOUCHED but ZERO lesson entries (KI/BP/agent-notes) updated in last 24h. Self-upgrade loop Stage 2 dormant. Per BP-S43b-4, append ≥1 entry before next /clear. AUTOMATED PATH: dispatch \\`lesson-synthesizer\\` subagent (.claude/agents/lesson-synthesizer.md) to extract patterns from session diff + write the entry; re-running this watchdog after dispatch should clear the alert.\"\n  printf '[%s] %s\\n' \"$TS\" \"$ALERT\" >> \"$LOG\"\n  printf '[%s] lesson-synthesis-watchdog: ALERT prod_touched=%s lessons=0\\n' \"$TS\" \"$PROD_TOUCHED\" >> \"$HOOK_LOG\"\n  echo \"$ALERT\" >&2\nfi\n\nexit 0\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":2,"oldLines":8,"newStart":2,"newLines":10,"lines":[" # lesson-synthesis-watchdog.sh — Stage 2 of self-upgrade loop (BP-S43b-4 / KI-S43b-5)."," #"," # Detects sessions that touched production code without appending ≥1 lesson entry","-# to known-issues.md / best-practices.md / agent-notes.md. Future LLM-perspective adapters (BC-8 today;\nany BC tomorrow that adds LLM extraction or classification) MUST adopt these\npatterns:\n\n- **Per-role model override** (BP-S43b-1): adapters expose `role_model_overrides`\n  so cost/latency-sensitive roles (e.g., Bull perspective) can downgrade Opus → Haiku\n  without touching call sites. Reference: `claude_llm_perspective_adapter.py`.\n- **Prose-tolerant JSON extractor** (BP-S43b-2): never call naive `json.loads`\n  on LLM output; use the 3-tier extractor (fenced block → first-`{` heuristic →\n  best-effort recovery). Reference: `subagent_transport.py:55-118`.\n- **Gatherer-wired deterministic compute** (BP-S43b-3): numbers come from code\n  (Charter Principle 9 / I-S1) — wire deterministic services (RatioService,\n  TaService, etc.) through the gatherer that prepares LLM context, not through\n  the LLM agent itself.\n\nKnown failure modes catalogued: KI-S43b-1 (sonnet pairing 300s subprocess timeout),\nKI-S43b-2 (LLM JSON in prose preamble), KI-S43b-3 (Windows cp1252 encoding crash).\nSee `agent-workspace/memory/self-awareness/{known-issues,best-practices}.md`.\n**Ratifying decision**: D-026 (S43e — bundled C1+C2 deny-lift cycle).\n\n### Frontend"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1265,"cache_read_input_tokens":100662,"output_tokens":1956,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1265,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[{"input_tokens":1,"output_tokens":1956,"cache_read_input_tokens":100662,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1265,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1265},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null},"requestId":"req_011CaiQrsFAkTzRKnEL9Y8eQ","type":"assistant","uuid":"b3467712-678a-4280-9843-7eb8bf18c542","timestamp":"2026-05-04T23:39:52.035Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"8888373d-50f1-4857-9d73-cab8e3902d6d","version":"2.1.124","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"266a8f74-e5c6-453d-8f9e-de945766a5ff","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-7","id":"msg_019cLq4ATPUYko8HgtcAjo5G","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01VT4yVgZnoYpgkse7GoExXr","name":"Edit","input":{"replace_all":false,"file_path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\agent-workspace\\constitution\\decision-discipline.md","old_string":"**Anti-pattern**: silently dismissing the soft-warning across multiple sessions without action — that IS the META-skip pattern.\n\n## Rule 5 — Provenance Required on Every Decision","new_string":"**Anti-pattern**: silently dismissing the soft-warning across multiple sessions without action — that IS the META-skip pattern.\n\n### Rule 4b — Lesson-synthesis mandatory at session-end (S43e charter-promote)\n\nEvery session whose work produces ANY of the following triggers MUST append at\nleast one new entry to `agent-workspace/memory/self-awareness/known-issues.md`\nOR `agent-workspace/memory/self-awareness/best-practices.md` OR\n`agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md` BEFORE the checkpoint `latest.md` is\nwritten:\n\n  (a) ≥1 user correction (verbatim or paraphrased)\n  (b) ≥1 deferred-fix item (R-N / DEFER-S*-N)\n  (c) ≥1 substrate gap discovered (hook missing, contract unenforced, etc.)\n  (d) ≥1 charter-tier or SCOPE-tier decision authored\n  (e) ≥1 META_LOOP recovery action\n\nThe entry MUST cite at minimum: (i) verbatim trigger evidence; (ii) the rule it\ncodifies; (iii) anti-example (what the rule prevents); (iv) auto-detect path\n(hook / skill / charter). this cluster's hook+code mitigations already shipped at S43b; charter cross-ref makes the canonical reference durable)\n  related_existing_artifacts:\n    - packages/infrastructure/analysis/claude_llm_perspective_adapter.py  # role_model_overrides field (BP-S43b-1)\n    - packages/infrastructure/analysis/subagent_transport.py:55-118       # 3-tier JSON extractor (BP-S43b-2)\n    - apps/_shared/use_case_builder.py::_build_subagent_agents             # gatherer-wired compute (BP-S43b-3)\n---\n\n# Proposal: Architecture amendment C1 — LLM substrate boundary cross-ref\n\n> **Status**: DRAFT — proposed for charter ratification at user discretion.\n> **Tier**: CHARTER (architecture.md is constitution-tier; edit requires deny-lift cycle per S38 mechanism — same channel that ratified D-015..D-024 Phase 2 charter promotes).\n> **Required action**: User explicit letter pick per Q-B2 closure (charter-tier MUST require explicit accept; default-acceptance prohibited).\n> **Bundling opportunity**: Pair with C2 `proposals/decision-discipline-amendment-rule-4b.md` for a single-batch deny-lift cycle covering both Phase 2 close charter promotes.\n\n## Why this amendment exists\n\nS43b harness recovery (sandwich-dev + verifier across 5 sub-sessions) surfaced 3 known-issues + 3 best-practices specifically about the LLM substrate seam — the boundary where deterministic Python code meets the non-deterministic LLM call. All three best-practices have already shipped as production code (citations in frontmatter). What is missing is the **canonical pointer**: when a future BC adds an LLM-perspective adapter (BC-8 already shipped; future BCs may add their own — KOL summarization, news classification, pump narrative detection), where does the agent look to find these patterns?\n\nWithout a charter cross-ref, the patterns live only in `self-awareness/best-practices.md` (a long, append-only file) and in the production code itself. Discovery is grep-dependent, not architecture-document-driven.\n\n## Proposed amendment text\n\nAppend a new subsection to `agent-workspace/constitution/architecture.md` immediately after § \"LLM\" (currently lines 124-131, between \"OSS fallback\" line and \"### Frontend\" line):\n\n```markdown\n### LLM Substrate Boundary\n\nThe boundary where deterministic Python code calls into a non-deterministic LLM\nis a **failure-prone seam** — Phase 2 (S43b) surfaced 3 distinct failure modes\nand shipped 3 mitigation patterns. Future LLM-perspective adapters (BC-8 today;\nany BC tomorrow that adds LLM extraction or classification) MUST adopt these\npatterns:\n\n- **Per-role model override** (BP-S43b-1): adapters expose `role_model_overrides`\n  so cost/latency-sensitive roles (e.g., Bull perspective) can downgrade Opus → Haiku\n  without touching call sites. Reference: `claude_llm_perspective_adapter.py`.\n- **Prose-tolerant JSON extractor** (BP-S43b-2): never call naive `json.loads`\n  on LLM output; use the 3-tier extractor (fenced block → first-`{` heuristic →\n  best-effort recovery). Reference: `subagent_transport.py:55-118`.\n- **Gatherer-wired deterministic compute** (BP-S43b-3): numbers come from code\n  (Charter Principle 9 / I-S1) — wire deterministic services (RatioService,\n  TaService, etc.) through the gatherer that prepares LLM context, not through\n  the LLM agent itself.\n\nKnown failure modes catalogued: KI-S43b-1 (sonnet pairing 300s subprocess timeout),\nKI-S43b-2 (LLM JSON in prose preamble), KI-S43b-3 (Windows cp1252 encoding crash).\nSee `agent-workspace/memory/self-awareness/{known-issues,best-practices}.md`.\n```\n\nTotal: ~22 LOC including header + bullets + references. Promote-rule estimate of \"~6 LOC\" understated the cite density required for the cross-ref to be navigable; this draft errs on the side of completeness.\n\n## Why charter-tier (not skill, not just hook)\n\nPer Q-E3 promotion priority — hook FIRST, skill SECOND, charter LAST. This cluster lands at charter because:\n\n1. **Hook tier already DONE implicitly**: the 3 mitigations are baked into production code paths; no separate hook needed because the patterns ARE the code.\n2. **Skill tier inappropriate**: this is not a procedure (no LLM-judgment-required steps); it's a structural reference for \"where do I look when adding an LLM-perspective adapter\". That's architecture-document territory.\n3. **Charter cross-ref is the durable form**: future-Claude reading architecture.md gets the pointer; future-Claude reading only `best-practices.md` may not realize these patterns are *required* for new LLM-perspective adapters, treating them as optional advice instead.\n\n## Trade-offs\n\n| Concern | Mitigation |\n|---|---|\n| **architecture.md grows over time as more substrate boundaries get cross-refs** | Acceptable; architecture.md is the canonical structural reference and IS supposed to enumerate substrate boundaries. The grow-rate is bounded by number of distinct failure-mode clusters surfaced (Phase 2 = 1 cluster; expect ~1 per phase). |\n| **Cross-ref text could go stale if BP-S43b-* IDs renumber** | Renumbering is forbidden by self-awareness append-only contract. IDs are stable for life of the project. |\n| **Future BCs may add patterns the cross-ref doesn't cover** | Each future cluster gets its own append at the same § \"LLM Substrate Boundary\" location; no rewrite of existing cite. |\n| **Charter-edit ceremony cost (deny-lift cycle)** | Bundle with C2 (Rule 4b) per \"Bundling opportunity\" above; 1 deny-lift cycle for both. |\n\n## Failure modes if NOT ratified\n\n- **Pattern rot**: future LLM-perspective adapters re-derive (or worse, omit) per-role override, prose-tolerant extractor, gatherer-wired compute. Each omission re-creates a KI-S43b-* class incident.\n- **Documentation fragmentation**: best-practices.md becomes the only source-of-truth pointer; agents consulting architecture.md get a wrong picture (LLM section says \"use Claude API\" but doesn't warn about the substrate failure modes).\n\n## What ratification looks like (for the user)\n\nIf the user picks \"ACCEPT\":\n1. Agent moves the amendment text from this proposal to `agent-workspace/constitution/architecture.md` via the S38 deny-lift mechanism (charter-edit gate).\n2. Insertion point: between current line 131 (\"OSS fallback (Phase 4+): Llama 3.3 70B via Ollama for cost reduction\") and current line 133 (\"### Frontend\").\n3. Agent authors `D-NNN-S43e-charter-promote-architecture-llm-substrate-boundary.md` ADR with approval_chain pointing to the user pick.\n\nIf the user picks \"REJECT\":\n1. Mark this proposal `status: REJECTED` with reason.\n2. Patterns continue to live only in `best-practices.md`; agent-notes.md retains the cluster.\n\nIf the user picks \"AMEND\":\n1. this cluster's hook+code mitigations already shipped at S43b; charter cross-ref makes the canonical reference durable)\n  related_existing_artifacts:\n    - packages/infrastructure/analysis/claude_llm_perspective_adapter.py  # role_model_overrides field (BP-S43b-1)\n    - packages/infrastructure/analysis/subagent_transport.py:55-118       # 3-tier JSON extractor (BP-S43b-2)\n    - apps/_shared/use_case_builder.py::_build_subagent_agents             # gatherer-wired compute (BP-S43b-3)\n---\n\n# Proposal: Architecture amendment C1 — LLM substrate boundary cross-ref\n\n> **Status**: DRAFT — proposed for charter ratification at user discretion.\n> **Tier**: CHARTER (architecture.md is constitution-tier; edit requires deny-lift cycle per S38 mechanism — same channel that ratified D-015..D-024 Phase 2 charter promotes).\n> **Required action**: User explicit letter pick per Q-B2 closure (charter-tier MUST require explicit accept; default-acceptance prohibited).\n> **Bundling opportunity**: Pair with C2 `proposals/decision-discipline-amendment-rule-4b.md` for a single-batch deny-lift cycle covering both Phase 2 close charter promotes.\n\n## Why this amendment exists\n\nS43b harness recovery (sandwich-dev + verifier across 5 sub-sessions) surfaced 3 known-issues + 3 best-practices specifically about the LLM substrate seam — the boundary where deterministic Python code meets the non-deterministic LLM call. All three best-practices have already shipped as production code (citations in frontmatter). What is missing is the **canonical pointer**: when a future BC adds an LLM-perspective adapter (BC-8 already shipped; future BCs may add their own — KOL summarization, news classification, pump narrative detection), where does the agent look to find these patterns?\n\nWithout a charter cross-ref, the patterns live only in `self-awareness/best-practices.md` (a long, append-only file) and in the production code itself. Discovery is grep-dependent, not architecture-document-driven.\n\n## Proposed amendment text\n\nAppend a new subsection to `agent-workspace/constitution/architecture.md` immediately after § \"LLM\" (currently lines 124-131, between \"OSS fallback\" line and \"### Frontend\" line):\n\n```markdown\n### LLM Substrate Boundary\n\nThe boundary where deterministic Python code calls into a non-deterministic LLM\nis a **failure-prone seam** — Phase 2 (S43b) surfaced 3 distinct failure modes\nand shipped 3 mitigation patterns. Future LLM-perspective adapters (BC-8 today;\nany BC tomorrow that adds LLM extraction or classification) MUST adopt these\npatterns:\n\n- **Per-role model override** (BP-S43b-1): adapters expose `role_model_overrides`\n  so cost/latency-sensitive roles (e.g., Bull perspective) can downgrade Opus → Haiku\n  without touching call sites. Reference: `claude_llm_perspective_adapter.py`.\n- **Prose-tolerant JSON extractor** (BP-S43b-2): never call naive `json.loads`\n  on LLM output; use the 3-tier extractor (fenced block → first-`{` heuristic →\n  best-effort recovery). Reference: `subagent_transport.py:55-118`.\n- **Gatherer-wired deterministic compute** (BP-S43b-3): numbers come from code\n  (Charter Principle 9 / I-S1) — wire deterministic services (RatioService,\n  TaService, etc.) through the gatherer that prepares LLM context, not through\n  the LLM agent itself.\n\nKnown failure modes catalogued: KI-S43b-1 (sonnet pairing 300s subprocess timeout),\nKI-S43b-2 (LLM JSON in prose preamble), KI-S43b-3 (Windows cp1252 encoding crash).\nSee `agent-workspace/memory/self-awareness/{known-issues,best-practices}.md`.\n```\n\nTotal: ~22 LOC including header + bullets + references. Promote-rule estimate of \"~6 LOC\" understated the cite density required for the cross-ref to be navigable; this draft errs on the side of completeness.\n\n## Why charter-tier (not skill, not just hook)\n\nPer Q-E3 promotion priority — hook FIRST, skill SECOND, charter LAST. This cluster lands at charter because:\n\n1. **Hook tier already DONE implicitly**: the 3 mitigations are baked into production code paths; no separate hook needed because the patterns ARE the code.\n2. **Skill tier inappropriate**: this is not a procedure (no LLM-judgment-required steps); it's a structural reference for \"where do I look when adding an LLM-perspective adapter\". That's architecture-document territory.\n3. **Charter cross-ref is the durable form**: future-Claude reading architecture.md gets the pointer; future-Claude reading only `best-practices.md` may not realize these patterns are *required* for new LLM-perspective adapters, treating them as optional advice instead.\n\n## Trade-offs\n\n| Concern | Mitigation |\n|---|---|\n| **architecture.md grows over time as more substrate boundaries get cross-refs** | Acceptable; architecture.md is the canonical structural reference and IS supposed to enumerate substrate boundaries. The grow-rate is bounded by number of distinct failure-mode clusters surfaced (Phase 2 = 1 cluster; expect ~1 per phase). |\n| **Cross-ref text could go stale if BP-S43b-* IDs renumber** | Renumbering is forbidden by self-awareness append-only contract. IDs are stable for life of the project. |\n| **Future BCs may add patterns the cross-ref doesn't cover** | Each future cluster gets its own append at the same § \"LLM Substrate Boundary\" location; no rewrite of existing cite. |\n| **Charter-edit ceremony cost (deny-lift cycle)** | Bundle with C2 (Rule 4b) per \"Bundling opportunity\" above; 1 deny-lift cycle for both. |\n\n## Failure modes if NOT ratified\n\n- **Pattern rot**: future LLM-perspective adapters re-derive (or worse, omit) per-role override, prose-tolerant extractor, gatherer-wired compute. Each omission re-creates a KI-S43b-* class incident.\n- **Documentation fragmentation**: best-practices.md becomes the only source-of-truth pointer; agents consulting architecture.md get a wrong picture (LLM section says \"use Claude API\" but doesn't warn about the substrate failure modes).\n\n## What ratification looks like (for the user)\n\nIf the user picks \"ACCEPT\":\n1. Agent moves the amendment text from this proposal to `agent-workspace/constitution/architecture.md` via the S38 deny-lift mechanism (charter-edit gate).\n2. Mark this proposal `status: REJECTED` with reason.\n2. Patterns continue to live only in `best-practices.md`; agent-notes.md retains the cluster.\n\nIf the user picks \"AMEND\":\n1. User specifies which clause to change (most likely candidate: shorten the amendment back toward the original \"~6 LOC\" target).\n2. KI-S35-5  # 15-session promote-skip\n    - BP-S35-1  # 5-session-or-phase-boundary\n    - KI-S43b-5  # 9-session lesson-synthesis dormancy\n    - BP-S43b-4  # lesson-synthesis mandatory\n    - L-S43b-7   # Lesson-Synthesis Stage 2 Of Self-Upgrade Loop Has No Agent\n  related_hooks_already_deployed:\n    - scripts/hooks/lesson-synthesis-watchdog.sh  # advisory mode (HR-1)\n    - scripts/hooks/promotion-cycle-trigger.sh    # delta-since-last hard-block at 5+\n    - scripts/hooks/harness-recovery-dod-watchdog.sh  # premature-stop sentinel\n    - scripts/hooks/memory-routing-audit.sh        # HR-4 routing-tree\n    - scripts/hooks/pre-clear-handoff-guard.sh     # HR-2 / HR-7\n---\n\n# Proposal: Decision-discipline Rule 4b — Lesson-synthesis mandatory at session-end\n\n> **Status**: DRAFT — proposed for charter ratification at user discretion.\n> **Tier**: CHARTER (per L-S15-1: any rule reshaping self-upgrade-loop identity is charter-tier).\n> **Required action**: User explicit letter pick per Q-B2 closure (charter/SCOPE-tier MUST require explicit accept; default-acceptance prohibited).\n\n## Why this rule exists\n\nThe self-upgrade loop (Karpathy outer-loop / decision-discipline § Rule 4) requires\nthat lessons learned in real sessions feed back into KI-* / BP-* / agent-notes\nentries, which then promote up to hooks / skills / charter via Rule 4 (5-session OR\nphase-boundary). Empirically, Stage 2 (the *write-the-lesson-down* step itself) has\nbeen the dormancy hotspot:\n\n- **S20 → S35**: 15 sessions elapsed before promote-rule fired (KI-S35-5).\n- **S26 → S43b**: 9 sessions elapsed before lesson-synthesizer ran (KI-S43b-5).\n- **L-S43b-7**: cataloged the failure mode — \"Stage 2 of Self-Upgrade Loop Has No Agent\".\n\nStage 1 (rule-discovery during work) is implicit in good engineering. Stage 2\n(rule-recording) is the bottleneck. Without a deterministic rule forcing it,\nsessions complete without synthesizing learnings, the corpus stagnates, and\npromote-rule cycles surface a thin set of stale candidates.\n\n## Proposed amendment text\n\nAppend to `agent-workspace/constitution/decision-discipline.md` § Rule 4 region:\n\n```markdown\n### Rule 4b — Lesson-synthesis mandatory at session-end\n\nEvery session whose work produces ANY of the following triggers MUST append at\nleast one new entry to `agent-workspace/memory/self-awareness/known-issues.md`\nOR `agent-workspace/memory/self-awareness/best-practices.md` OR\n`agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md` BEFORE the checkpoint `latest.md` is\nwritten:\n\n  (a) ≥1 user correction (verbatim or paraphrased)\n  (b) ≥1 deferred-fix item (R-N / DEFER-S*-N)\n  (c) ≥1 substrate gap discovered (hook missing, contract unenforced, etc.)\n  (d) ≥1 charter-tier or SCOPE-tier decision authored\n  (e) ≥1 META_LOOP recovery action\n\nThe entry MUST cite at minimum: (i) verbatim trigger evidence; (ii) the rule it\ncodifies; (iii) anti-example (what the rule prevents); (iv) auto-detect path\n(hook / skill / charter). Sessions producing zero triggers (e.g., rote refactor\nsessions) are exempt and SHOULD record `lesson_synthesis: NA-no-triggers` in\ntheir session log.\n\n**Enforcement** (paired hook upgrade):\n  - `scripts/hooks/lesson-synthesis-watchdog.sh` is promoted from advisory\n    (current default) to STRICT mode (exit 2 on dormancy detection).\n  - Strict mode auto-clears once the next session writes a qualifying entry.\n  - Loop is finite: ≤1 hard-block per dormancy episode.\n\n**Cross-references**: KI-S35-5, BP-S35-1, KI-S43b-5, BP-S43b-4, L-S43b-7.\n**Supersedes**: nothing (additive to Rule 4).\n**Companion**: Rule 4 promote-rule cadence remains 5-session OR phase-boundary;\nthis rule shortens the *upstream* feedback latency that feeds Rule 4.\n```\n\n## Why charter-tier (not skill, not just hook)\n\nPer Q-E3 promotion priority (closed S15) — hook FIRST, skill SECOND, charter LAST.\nThis proposal lands at charter because:\n\n1. **The hook already exists** (`lesson-synthesis-watchdog.sh`) but is advisory-only.\n   Promoting it to strict-mode requires a charter-tier rule to cite as authority.\n2. **The pattern reshapes self-upgrade-loop identity** — it codifies *that* the loop\n   has a Stage 2 obligation, not merely *how* to enforce it. That's identity-level\n   (per L-S15-1 charter-split rule).\n3. **Skill insufficient** — this is a discipline rule, not a procedure. There is no\n   sequence of LLM-judgment-required steps; the rule is \"write or be blocked\".\n\n## Trade-offs\n\n| Concern | Mitigation |\n|---|---|\n| **False-positive blocks on rote sessions** | Exemption clause `lesson_synthesis: NA-no-triggers` + 5 explicit trigger gates (a)-(e); rote refactor sessions self-attest exemption. |\n| **Verbose KI/BP corpus growth** | Rule 4 promote-rule cadence (5-session OR phase-boundary) prunes via cluster-and-promote; growth pressure is already balanced by demote pressure. |\n| **Strict-mode hard-block surprise** | Loop is finite (≤1 per episode); exit 2 surfaces stderr to assistant transcript per HR-7 pattern; agent writes entry → next Stop auto-clears. |\n| **Watchdog itself dormant** | Hook is in `.claude/settings.json` Stop chain priority 12 (already deployed); strict-mode upgrade is a 1-line change in the script. |\n\n## Failure modes if NOT ratified\n\n- Recurrence: 6+ sessions of dormancy expected within next phase based on KI-S43b-5\n  empirical baseline.\n- Compounding: stale promote-rule candidate pool → low-quality cluster proposals →\n  stale charter → meta-loop trust loss (per L-S43b-10 premature-stop family).\n\n## What ratification looks like (for the user)\n\nIf the user picks \"ACCEPT\":\n1. Agent moves this file to `agent-workspace/constitution/decision-discipline.md` via\n   the S38 deny-lift mechanism (charter-edit gate).\n2. Agent appends the amendment text verbatim under § Rule 4 region.\n3. Agent flips `lesson-synthesis-watchdog.sh` from advisory to strict (1-line edit:\n   `exit 0` → `exit 2` on dormancy branch).\n4. Agent authors `D-NNN-decision-discipline-rule-4b-ratified.md` ADR with\n   approval_chain pointing to the user pick.\n\nIf the user picks \"REJECT\":\n1. Mark this proposal `status: REJECTED` with reason.\n2. Continue advisory-mode watchdog indefinitely.\n3. Re-propose only if BP-S43b-4 violation recurs ≥3× within next phase.\n\nIf the user picks \"AMEND\":\n1. User specifies which clause to change.\n2. Paired hook\n`scripts/hooks/lesson-synthesis-watchdog.sh` flipped advisory→strict same turn.\nBundled with C1 in single deny-lift cycle.\nRatifying ADR: `agent-workspace/memory/decisions/026-S43e-charter-promote-bundle-C1-C2.md`.","originalFile":"---\nproposal_id: decision-discipline-amendment-rule-4b\ntitle: Decision-discipline Rule 4b — Lesson-synthesis mandatory at session-end (charter-tier amendment draft)\nstatus: ACCEPTED\ndraft_date: 2026-05-04\ndraft_session: S43e\nauthoring_agent: Claude Opus 4.7\ntarget_charter_file: agent-workspace/constitution/decision-discipline.md\ngating: USER-EXPLICIT-PICK-REQUIRED (per Q-B2 charter-tier rule + L-S15-1)\nprovenance:\n  promote_rule_observation: agent-workspace/memory/observations/promote-rule-S43c.md § Cluster C2\n  source_rules:\n    - KI-S35-5  # 15-session promote-skip\n    - BP-S35-1  # 5-session-or-phase-boundary\n    - KI-S43b-5  # 9-session lesson-synthesis dormancy\n    - BP-S43b-4  # lesson-synthesis mandatory\n    - L-S43b-7   # Lesson-Synthesis Stage 2 Of Self-Upgrade Loop Has No Agent\n  related_hooks_already_deployed:\n    - scripts/hooks/lesson-synthesis-watchdog.sh  # advisory mode (HR-1)\n    - scripts/hooks/promotion-cycle-trigger.sh    # delta-since-last hard-block at 5+\n    - scripts/hooks/harness-recovery-dod-watchdog.sh  # premature-stop sentinel\n    - scripts/hooks/memory-routing-audit.sh        # HR-4 routing-tree\n    - scripts/hooks/pre-clear-handoff-guard.sh     # HR-2 / HR-7\n---\n\n# Proposal: Decision-discipline Rule 4b — Lesson-synthesis mandatory at session-end\n\n> **Status**: DRAFT — proposed for charter ratification at user discretion.\n> **Tier**: CHARTER (per L-S15-1: any rule reshaping self-upgrade-loop identity is charter-tier).\n> **Required action**: User explicit letter pick per Q-B2 closure (charter/SCOPE-tier MUST require explicit accept; default-acceptance prohibited).\n\n## Why this rule exists\n\nThe self-upgrade loop (Karpathy outer-loop / decision-discipline § Rule 4) requires\nthat lessons learned in real sessions feed back into KI-* / BP-* / agent-notes\nentries, which then promote up to hooks / skills / charter via Rule 4 (5-session OR\nphase-boundary). Empirically, Stage 2 (the *write-the-lesson-down* step itself) has\nbeen the dormancy hotspot:\n\n- **S20 → S35**: 15 sessions elapsed before promote-rule fired (KI-S35-5).\n- **S26 → S43b**: 9 sessions elapsed before lesson-synthesizer ran (KI-S43b-5).\n- **L-S43b-7**: cataloged the failure mode — \"Stage 2 of Self-Upgrade Loop Has No Agent\".\n\nStage 1 (rule-discovery during work) is implicit in good engineering. Stage 2\n(rule-recording) is the bottleneck. Without a deterministic rule forcing it,\nsessions complete without synthesizing learnings, the corpus stagnates, and\npromote-rule cycles surface a thin set of stale candidates.\n\n## Proposed amendment text\n\nAppend to `agent-workspace/constitution/decision-discipline.md` § Rule 4 region:\n\n```markdown\n### Rule 4b — Lesson-synthesis mandatory at session-end\n\nEvery session whose work produces ANY of the following triggers MUST append at\nleast one new entry to `agent-workspace/memory/self-awareness/known-issues.md`\nOR `agent-workspace/memory/self-awareness/best-practices.md` OR\n`agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md` BEFORE the checkpoint `latest.md` is\nwritten:\n\n  (a) ≥1 user correction (verbatim or paraphrased)\n  (b) ≥1 deferred-fix item (R-N / DEFER-S*-N)\n  (c) ≥1 substrate gap discovered (hook missing, contract unenforced, etc.)\n  (d) ≥1 charter-tier or SCOPE-tier decision authored\n  (e) ≥1 META_LOOP recovery action\n\nThe entry MUST cite at minimum: (i) verbatim trigger evidence; (ii) the rule it\ncodifies; (iii) anti-example (what the rule prevents); (iv) auto-detect path\n(hook / skill / charter). Sessions producing zero triggers (e.g., rote refactor\nsessions) are exempt and SHOULD record `lesson_synthesis: NA-no-triggers` in\ntheir session log.\n\n**Enforcement** (paired hook upgrade):\n  - `scripts/hooks/lesson-synthesis-watchdog.sh` is promoted from advisory\n    (current default) to STRICT mode (exit 2 on dormancy detection).\n  - Strict mode auto-clears once the next session writes a qualifying entry.\n  - Loop is finite: ≤1 hard-block per dormancy episode.\n\n**Cross-references**: KI-S35-5, BP-S35-1, KI-S43b-5, BP-S43b-4, L-S43b-7.\n**Supersedes**: nothing (additive to Rule 4).\n**Companion**: Rule 4 promote-rule cadence remains 5-session OR phase-boundary;\nthis rule shortens the *upstream* feedback latency that feeds Rule 4.\n```\n\n## Why charter-tier (not skill, not just hook)\n\nPer Q-E3 promotion priority (closed S15) — hook FIRST, skill SECOND, charter LAST.\nThis proposal lands at charter because:\n\n1. **The hook already exists** (`lesson-synthesis-watchdog.sh`) but is advisory-only.\n   Promoting it to strict-mode requires a charter-tier rule to cite as authority.\n2. **The pattern reshapes self-upgrade-loop identity** — it codifies *that* the loop\n   has a Stage 2 obligation, not merely *how* to enforce it. That's identity-level\n   (per L-S15-1 charter-split rule).\n3. **Skill insufficient** — this is a discipline rule, not a procedure. There is no\n   sequence of LLM-judgment-required steps; the rule is \"write or be blocked\".\n\n## Trade-offs\n\n| Concern | Mitigation |\n|---|---|\n| **False-positive blocks on rote sessions** | Exemption clause `lesson_synthesis: NA-no-triggers` + 5 explicit trigger gates (a)-(e); rote refactor sessions self-attest exemption. |\n| **Verbose KI/BP corpus growth** | Rule 4 promote-rule cadence (5-session OR phase-boundary) prunes via cluster-and-promote; growth pressure is already balanced by demote pressure. |\n| **Strict-mode hard-block surprise** | Loop is finite (≤1 per episode); exit 2 surfaces stderr to assistant transcript per HR-7 pattern; agent writes entry → next Stop auto-clears. |\n| **Watchdog itself dormant** | Hook is in `.claude/settings.json` Stop chain priority 12 (already deployed); strict-mode upgrade is a 1-line change in the script. |\n\n## Failure modes if NOT ratified\n\n- Recurrence: 6+ sessions of dormancy expected within next phase based on KI-S43b-5\n  empirical baseline.\n- Compounding: stale promote-rule candidate pool → low-quality cluster proposals →\n  stale charter → meta-loop trust loss (per L-S43b-10 premature-stop family).\n\n## What ratification looks like (for the user)\n\nIf the user picks \"ACCEPT\":\n1. Agent moves this file to `agent-workspace/constitution/decision-discipline.md` via\n   the S38 deny-lift mechanism (charter-edit gate).\n2. Agent appends the amendment text verbatim under § Rule 4 region.\n3. Agent flips `lesson-synthesis-watchdog.sh` from advisory to strict (1-line edit:\n   `exit 0` → `exit 2` on dormancy branch).\n4. Agent authors `D-NNN-decision-discipline-rule-4b-ratified.md` ADR with\n   approval_chain pointing to the user pick.\n\nIf the user picks \"REJECT\":\n1. Mark this proposal `status: REJECTED` with reason.\n2. Continue advisory-mode watchdog indefinitely.\n3. Re-propose only if BP-S43b-4 violation recurs ≥3× within next phase.\n\nIf the user picks \"AMEND\":\n1. User specifies which clause to change.\n2. Agent revises this proposal; re-presents.\n\n## Related open proposals (sibling-cluster context)\n\n- `proposals/architecture-amendment.md` — adjacent self-upgrade-loop articulation.\n- `proposals/session-budgets-amendment.md` — sibling discipline rule on token budgets.\n\n## Ratification record\n\n(Empty until user pick lands.)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":139,"oldLines":4,"newStart":139,"newLines":9,"lines":[" "," ## Ratification record"," ","-(Empty until user pick lands.)","+**ACCEPTED** 2026-05-05 (S43f turn) via AskUserQuestion bundle Q2=ACCEPT.","+Charter edit applied to `agent-workspace/constitution/decision-discipline.md`","+§ Rule 4 region (after Rule 4a, before Rule 5). Author\n`agent-workspace/session-plans/pending/007-S44-phase-3-master-plan.md` via\nmaster-planner subagent dispatch (per S31 Phase 2 master-plan precedent).\n\n## Q4 — DEFER-S43b-2 closure as Option A\n\n**Closure rationale**: 6 dogfood runs in Phase 2 (BID + CTG + 4 others)\nempirically demonstrate that bank-sector tickers are handled correctly by\nRule-7 narrative honest-insufficient. RatioService returns `None` for\ninapplicable bank ratios (debt/equity, current-ratio); the LLM perspective\nadapter renders this as data-gap-attributed-emptiness (per L-S43e-1 § Path A\nsubstrate-not-bug taxonomy).\n\n**No Phase 3 schema work scheduled**. Bank-specific ratio adapter (NPL ratio,\nNIM, CAR, LDR) and generic sector router are NOT in Phase 3 scope.\n\n**Re-open conditions**: if Phase 3 dogfood reveals systematic VF-5 detector\nblindness on bank-sector tickers (≥3 runs producing 0/5 disagreements with\ndata-gap attribution AND user judgment that 0/5 is unacceptable), then\nre-propose as SCOPE-tier amendment for Phase 4.\n\n**DEFER-S43b-2 status**: ✅ CLOSED — Option A (keep doctrine) ratified\n2026-05-05 user pick.\n\n## Self-upgrade-loop Stage 2 obligation (Rule 4b just-ratified)\n\nThis turn produced:\n- (d) ≥1 charter-tier decision authored — D-026 (C1 + C2 bundle)\n- (b) ≥1 deferred-fix item resolved — DEFER-S43b-2 closed\n\nRule 4b (just-ratified D-026) requires ≥1 KI/BP/agent-notes entry before next\ncheckpoint write. This observation file is NOT itself a Rule 4b entry — must\nappend to `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md` separately.\n\n**L-S43f-1 candidate**: \"Bundled deny-lift cycle for sibling charter-tier\nproposals\" — when ≥2 charter-tier proposals are pending and target distinct\nfiles, ratify in single AskUserQuestion bundle + single deny-lift cycle to\namortize permission ceremony cost. {"parentUuid":"d9498fae-7e64-4dd9-8395-5ae8c2ce39e1","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"00fd1af7-4b67-45ee-9a33-1a3c6db1c2e5","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Dqp5xMRYMjmtT5RotxeFNa","type":"tool_result","content":"The file C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\agent-workspace\\proposals\\architecture-amendment.md has been updated successfully."}]},"uuid":"d201d220-103a-4757-b547-e1bc6e2c296f","timestamp":"2026-05-04T23:46:57.879Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\agent-workspace\\proposals\\architecture-amendment.md","oldString":"status: PROPOSAL — AMENDMENT to existing agent-workspace/constitution/architecture.md","newString":"status: ACCEPTED (ratified S43c via D-018; frontmatter sync S43f)","originalFile":"---\nstatus: PROPOSAL — AMENDMENT to existing agent-workspace/constitution/architecture.md\nproposed_at: 2026-04-29\nproposed_by: Claude Opus 4.7 (S16 IMPL — Track 7 ratification)\nsource_evidence:\n  - agent-notes.md § L-S14-2 (skill-vs-command duplication multiplier)\n  - session-plans/pending/003-S15-track-7-constitution-amendments.md § 2 + § 4.2\ntarget_constitution_path: agent-workspace/constitution/architecture.md\ntarget_section: NEW § \"Slash Command vs Skill — Responsibility Split\"\nmove_when: user explicit approve; insertion point = after \"## Forbidden Patterns\" section, before \"## Evolution Protocol\"\n---\n\n# Architecture Amendment — Slash Command vs Skill Responsibility Split\n\n> **Status**: PROPOSAL pending user approval. Per `agent-workspace/CLAUDE.md` rule 1, agents WRITE to `proposals/`; user approve appends this delta to `agent-workspace/constitution/architecture.md`.\n\n## Append to `architecture.md` (NEW section, after Forbidden Patterns)\n\n---\n\n## Slash Command vs Skill — Responsibility Split\n\nSlash commands (`.claude/commands/<name>.md`) and skills (`.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`) overlap in form (both are markdown procedure files) but should NOT overlap in responsibility. Per L-S14-2 (skill-vs-command duplication multiplier), duplicating procedure between a `/foo` command and a `foo` skill multiplies maintenance cost AND creates drift between the two when one updates and the other doesn't.\n\n### Responsibility Split\n\n| Concern | Slash Command | Skill |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Trigger** | User explicit invocation: `/<name>` | Auto-discovered by Claude Code via `description:` keyword match |\n| **Audience** | User-facing workflow (command sequence to execute) | Agent-facing procedure (rules to follow when context matches) |\n| **Body shape** | \"When user types `/<name>`, do these N steps\" — imperative checklist | \"When working in context X, follow this discipline\" — declarative rules |\n| **Reusability** | Single workflow tied to a slash invocation | Reusable across many tasks that match the description |\n| **LOC ceiling** | 120 (per drift-signals D1) | 150 (per drift-signals D1) |\n\n### Anti-Pattern: Duplicated Body\n\nIf `/<name>` command and `<name>` skill both exist with overlapping body content, the skill MUST be the source of truth and the command body MUST delegate (e.g., the command body says \"invokes `<name>` skill via Skill tool\" or copy-references the skill's authoritative rules).\n\n**Example (correct)**: `/grill-me` command body is short — describes user-facing trigger; the procedure lives in `grill-maximization` skill, which the command references.\n\n**Example (anti-pattern)**: `/grill-me` command body and `grill-maximization` skill both contain a 80-line \"how to bundle questions\" procedure. When the bundling rule changes (e.g., 4-question max per AskUserQuestion limit), only one gets updated. The drift signal D-DUPL (TBD) flags >50% line overlap between command + skill of similar name.\n\n### Boundary Heuristics\n\n- If the procedure runs once per user invocation → slash command\n- If the procedure runs across many tasks based on context auto-match → skill\n- If both apply: skill carries the body; command is the entry point\n\n## When SKILL.md Exceeds Ceiling — Companion-via-References (L-S16-1, applied S20)\n\nPer drift-signals D1, SKILL.md ceiling is 150 LOC. When a skill's procedure genuinely needs more body than fits, split content to `references/<topic>.md` companion files; SKILL.md keeps the high-density rules + delegates detail.\n\n**Pattern**:\n- SKILL.md body: rules / when-to-use / anti-patterns (≤150 LOC)\n- `references/<topic>.md`: extended templates / examples / sub-rules (no LOC ceiling)\n\n**Examples (Track 6 secondary closure S20)**:\n- `spec-to-wiki/SKILL.md` 227 → 67 LOC; companion `references/templates.md` 163 LOC consolidating 5 sub-templates\n- `ubiquitous-language/SKILL.md` 210 → 97 LOC; companion `references/templates.md` 120 LOC schema + examples + drift-log\n- `write-a-skill/SKILL.md` 163 → 99 LOC; companion `references/templates.md` 88 LOC SKILL skeleton + failure modes\n\n**When NOT to split**: if compression by prose paraphrasing keeps body ≤ ceiling without losing content, prefer compression over split (Phase 0 portability principle: fewer files = less drift surface). Examples shipped self-contained: `crawler-reliability/SKILL.md` 226 → 102, `fastapi-module/SKILL.md` 225 → 122.\n\n**Anti-pattern**: creating `references/` companion file for content that compresses cleanly into prose. Adds file to track without information gain.\n\n## When Porting From Source Repos — Cross-Locale Pattern Extension (L-S18-1, S18 evidence)\n\nWhen porting a regex-based extractor (or any pattern-matcher whose patterns hard-code language-specific terms) from a source repo to stockforge, the regex set is NOT portable — it is locale-sensitive.\n\n**Pattern**: source repo patterns serve source locale; stockforge user is Vietnamese-speaking. Direct port without locale extension yields false-negative on Vietnamese failure phrases.\n\n**Example (Track 8b S18)**: ported `extract_l0.py` from `C:/htdocs/orch-starter`; English-only `\\b(failed|stuck|broken|error)\\b` patterns missed Vietnamese. Added 5 NEW patterns: `bị lỗi` / `mắc kẹt` / `không hoạt động` / `thất bại` / `bug` (loanword). Bilingual extractor without requiring NLP model.\n\n**Discipline**: when porting any locale-sensitive pattern set (regex / keyword list / stop-list / sentiment lexicon), pre-flight checklist MUST include:\n1. List regex/keywords in source\n2. Translate to target locale (Vietnamese for stockforge)\n3. Add target-locale patterns alongside source-locale (bilingual; don't replace)\n4. Test on locale-specific corpus before declaring port complete\n\n**Anti-pattern**: assuming portability based on language semantics (\"regex is language-agnostic\"). The SYNTAX is agnostic; the CONTENT isn't.\n\n## Telemetry Rollup Design — Deterministic Aggregator Before LLM Guardian (L-S19-1, S19 evidence)\n\nFor session-level telemetry rollup (aggregating per-session metrics across many sessions for self-awareness profile), prefer **deterministic Stop-hook aggregator** over **continuous LLM Guardian** as Phase 0 implementation.\n\n**Pattern**:\n- Deterministic aggregator: bash + awk parsing JSONL/TSV at session-end; runs in milliseconds; emits a row to sessions-rollup.tsv. Cost: ~zero LLM tokens; deterministic output; auditable.\n- LLM Guardian: continuous polling + analysis subagent. Cost: ~1-5K tokens per poll; non-deterministic; not auditable without persistence.\n\n**Phase 0 verdict (Track 9 S19)**: deterministic aggregator wins for rollup use case. LLM Guardian reserves itself for **end-of-phase analysis** (when accumulated rollup data needs interpretation, not collection).\n\n**Example**: `scripts/hooks/self-awareness-aggregate.sh` 124 LOC bash+awk only. Reads dispatch.jsonl + component-telemetry.jsonl + .transcript-tokens + .session-hooks.log + sessions/*.md → emits 1 row to sessions-rollup.tsv. Smoke-tested S19; PASS.\n\n**Anti-pattern (already AP-23 catalogued)**: \"Continuous LLM-Guardian\" — running a polling subagent that watches for telemetry events and synthesizes rollup. Wastes tokens; non-deterministic; cost grows with session length. Reserve LLM analysis for batch end-of-phase rollup interpretation, not real-time aggregation.\n\n**Boundary**: aggregator = collection-only (deterministic); LLM analysis = interpretation-only (over deterministic corpus, batch form, when needed).\n\n## End of amendment\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":5,"newStart":1,"newLines":5,"lines":[" ---","-status: PROPOSAL — AMENDMENT to existing agent-workspace/constitution/architecture.md","+status: ACCEPTED (ratified S43c via D-018; frontmatter sync S43f)"," proposed_at: 2026-04-29"," proposed_by: Claude Opus 4.7 (S16 IMPL — Track 7 ratification)"," source_evidence:"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"d9498fae-7e64-4dd9-8395-5ae8c2ce39e1","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"8888373d-50f1-4857-9d73-cab8e3902d6d","version":"2.1.124","gitBranch":"main"}

Codifies the existing L-S11-1 doctrine (Phase 0 hooks must be bash + POSIX only) as a financial-data-protocol clause because hook portability is a precondition for the data-integrity rules in Rules 1-10.\n\n## Append to `financial-data-protocol.md` (NEW section)\n\n---\n\n## Rule 11 — Hook Portability Per Phase\n\nThe data-integrity hooks in `scripts/hooks/` (telemetry, drift signals, learning-data sweepers, citation grep) enforce Rules 1-10. They must remain portable across phase boundaries so a fresh project clone reproduces the same enforcement without external toolchain installation.\n\n### Phase 0 (Harness Bootstrap) — bash + POSIX only\n\nDuring Phase 0, hooks MUST use bash + POSIX utilities only. Forbidden: `python`/`python3`, `jq`/`yq`, `pip`/`npm`/`pnpm`. Reason: a fresh user cloning the repo at Phase 0 has not yet provisioned a Python venv or jq install; hook failures at SessionStart create a worse first impression than no hook.\n\n**Enforcement**: `scripts/hooks/bash-hook-lint.sh § Check 1 L-S11-1` scans `scripts/hooks/*.sh` and soft-warns on any non-Phase-0-portable invocation.\n\n### Phase 1+ (Data Pipeline Active) — Python + jq accepted\n\nOnce Phase 1 ships the Python venv + data dependencies (`pyproject.toml` provisioned), hooks may invoke Python and jq. The bash-hook-lint check downgrades L-S11-1 to informational severity at phase boundary (config flag: `STOCKFORGE_HOOK_PORTABILITY_TIER=1`).\n\n### Why This Matters for Financial Data Integrity\n\nA Phase 0 hook that depends on jq for JSON parsing fails silently when jq is missing. Silent hook failure = drift signal not firing = data-integrity violation goes undetected. The portability rule is upstream of every Rule 1-10 enforcement.\n\n**Concrete example**: D9 drift signal (runtime-path-leak into `learning-data/(events|archive)/`) is critical for Rule 6 (LLM Output Provenance) — if D9 hook fails to run because of a missing dependency, runtime code can silently load write-only telemetry into reasoning context, polluting decisions with non-runtime data.\n\n## End of amendment\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":5,"newStart":1,"newLines":5,"lines":[" ---","-status: PROPOSAL — AMENDMENT to existing agent-workspace/constitution/financial-data-protocol.md","+status: ACCEPTED (ratified S43c via D-019; frontmatter sync S43f)"," proposed_at: 2026-04-29"," proposed_by: Claude Opus 4.7 (S16 IMPL — Track 7 ratification)"," source_evidence:"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"0f5c4cb4-c386-4303-9baa-9169e6b37730","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"8888373d-50f1-4857-9d73-cab8e3902d6d","version":"2.1.124","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"1f25addc-1d57-4905-a1d5-3001566832f8","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"00fd1af7-4b67-45ee-9a33-1a3c6db1c2e5","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_013gzDboApGQLF7xfB21ZmKn","type":"tool_result","content":"The file C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\agent-workspace\\proposals\\session-budgets-amendment.md has been updated successfully."}]},"uuid":"b2e55eb5-12fc-4c7f-adeb-538ad213966a","timestamp":"2026-05-04T23:47:15.681Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\agent-workspace\\proposals\\session-budgets-amendment.md","oldString":"status: PROPOSAL — AMENDMENT to existing agent-workspace/constitution/session-budgets.md","newString":"status: ACCEPTED (ratified S43c via D-020; frontmatter sync S43f)","originalFile":"---\nstatus: PROPOSAL — AMENDMENT to existing agent-workspace/constitution/session-budgets.md\nproposed_at: 2026-04-29\nproposed_by: Claude Opus 4.7 (S16 IMPL — Track 7 ratification)\nsource_evidence:\n  - agent-notes.md § L-S14-4 (autonomous_mode flag + Mode-D clean-handoff coverage; cliff-vs-injector dispatch)\n  - session-plans/pending/003-S15-track-7-constitution-amendments.md § 2 + § 4.2\n  - decisions/004-up07-context-threshold-opus47.md (Opus 4.7 thresholds 180K/220K/250K)\ntarget_constitution_path: agent-workspace/constitution/session-budgets.md\ntarget_section: NEW § \"Mode A/B/C/D — Cliff vs Injector Dispatch\"\nmove_when: user explicit approve; insertion point = after \"## Hard Rules\" section, before \"## When to Escalate\"\n---\n\n# Session Budgets Amendment — Cliff vs Injector Dispatch\n\n> **Status**: PROPOSAL pending user approval. Codifies the autonomous-loop handoff dispatch logic shipped in S14 (`autonomous-stop-watchdog.sh` + `continue-injector.ps1`) as a budget-discipline clause.\n\n## Append to `session-budgets.md` (NEW section)\n\n---\n\n## Mode A/B/C/D — Cliff vs Injector Dispatch\n\nPer Opus 4.7 thresholds (D-004): wind-down at 180K / cliff at 220K / hard cap at 250K. The autonomous loop's handoff mechanism depends on which threshold the session crossed.\n\n### Mode A — Stop without budget alert\n\n`autonomous-stop-watchdog.sh` writes a minimal continue prompt; user's terminal pulls via `continue-injector.ps1` to resume mid-session. Same context window continues.\n\n### Mode B — Cliff reached (≥220K), session must reboot\n\n`budget-watchdog.sh` triggers `session-self-reboot.sh`. Fresh context window starts; new session reads `checkpoints/latest.md` to resume.\n\n**Reason for fresh-context**: past 220K, transformer attention degrades (per session-budgets.md § Quality Cliff). Continuing in the same context produces \"lost in the middle\" effect; agent forgets rules. Fresh context is cheaper than degraded output.\n\n### Mode C — Premature wind-down before cliff\n\n`budget-watchdog.sh` flags mode-C event in JSONL telemetry (`failure_mode: C` per D-003 § 5.5c.5 REV-4); handoff prep proceeds; user resumes via continue-injector.\n\n### Mode D — Clean handoff (S14 addition, L-S14-4)\n\n`autonomous-stop-watchdog.sh` recognizes intentional close — checkpoint mtime ≤ 60 seconds AND no A/B/C alert fired. Resume reads `checkpoints/latest.md` cleanly. JSONL `failure_mode: D` (NOT a failure; \"D = clean handoff\").\n\n### Dispatch Rule\n\n```\nbudget < 180K + checkpoint fresh                     → Mode D (clean)\nbudget < 180K + no checkpoint                        → Mode A (continue-injector mid-session)\n180K ≤ budget < 220K                                  → Mode C (wind-down; handoff prep)\nbudget ≥ 220K                                        → Mode B (cliff; session-self-reboot fresh ctx)\n```\n\nThe choice between continue-injector (same-context resume) vs session-self-reboot (fresh-context restart) is **deterministic per the budget threshold**, not per agent judgment.\n\n## Verifier Budget by Scope (L-S21-1, S21 verifier evidence)\n\nSandwich-verifier dispatch budget depends on artifact-set scope:\n\n| Scope | Token cap | Use case |\n|---|---|---|\n| Single-track (1-3 sessions, 1 decision) | 60-80K | Per-track close verification |\n| Multi-track (5-10 sessions, 2-3 decisions) | 100-120K | Mid-phase checkpoint review |\n| Whole-Phase (≥15 sessions, ≥5 decisions, full artifact set) | **150K** | Phase-boundary final verifier |\n\n**Why 150K for whole-Phase**: S21 verifier covering V1-V10 dimensions across 19 sessions + 8 decisions + 7 proposals + 9 constitution files + 31 hooks + 25 skills + 15 commands + 9 agents + Python library consumed 126K tokens / 89 tool uses / 9.7 minutes. Initial 80K cap forced verdict + V1-V10 covered but at cost of incomplete tail; budget calibration to 150K avoids partial-completion noise.\n\n**Discipline**:\n- Pre-dispatch: estimate artifact LOC + count files; if ≥10K LOC + ≥30 files, target whole-Phase budget (150K).\n- Mid-dispatch: if verifier returns \"partial\", accept if verdict + all 10 dimensions covered; do NOT re-dispatch for marginal completeness gain.\n- Post-dispatch: log actual tokens + tool uses for future calibration.\n\n**Anti-pattern**: re-dispatching a verifier that delivered verdict + all V1-V10 just because token count exceeded cap. Wasted tokens; output already sufficient.\n\n## End of amendment\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":5,"newStart":1,"newLines":5,"lines":[" ---","-status: PROPOSAL — AMENDMENT to existing agent-workspace/constitution/session-budgets.md","+status: ACCEPTED (ratified S43c via D-020; frontmatter sync S43f)"," proposed_at: 2026-04-29"," proposed_by: Claude Opus 4.7 (S16 IMPL — Track 7 ratification)"," source_evidence:"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"1f25addc-1d57-4905-a1d5-3001566832f8","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"8888373d-50f1-4857-9d73-cab8e3902d6d","version":"2.1.124","gitBranch":"main"}
